Judgment

This is a charge sheet filed by the PSI of VV Puram police station Station, Bengaluru against the accused for the offence punishable U/sec.51 (B), 63 of Copy Right Act and Sec.420 of IPC.
02.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the prosecution case is that, the accused was found selling duplicate HP printer on foot path near Sajjan Rao Circle, Bengaluru on 13.06.2019 at 2 pm and he stored duplicate HP cartridges and MRP stickers in his godown situated at KR Puram in Ayyappa building and thus the accused has found selling duplicate HP toner by infringing the copy right by using the logo and design of HP company and thus the accused has violated the copy right and also cheated the public at large and thus the accused has committed the offences U/Sec.51(B), 63 of Copy Right Act and Sec.
420 of IPC.
03.

After filing of charge sheet, this court took cognizance for the offences punishable U/sec.51(B)
63 of Copy Right Act and issued summons to the accused.
Accordingly the accused appeared before the court through his counsel and enlarged on bail.

Later on, charge sheet copy and prosecution papers were furnished to the accused under Sec.207 of Cr.P.C.
04.
Heard both side on framing of charge, perused the prosecution papers.

As there are sufficient materials to frame the charge against the accused, the charges has been framed for the offence punishable U/Sec. 420 of I.P.C., along with U/sec.51(B) 63 of Copy Right Act and the same were read over to him, but he denied the contents of charge and claimed for trial.
Hence, the case was posted for prosecution evidence.
05. In furtherance of the charges leveled against the accused, the following points are arisen for my consideration.
POINTS 01.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused was found selling duplicate HP printer on foot path near Sajjan Rao Circle, Bengaluru on 13.06.2019 at 2 pm and he Samir Shaw vs Babu Khan on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111909153/
2 was found stored duplicate HP cartridges and MRP stickers in his godown situated at KR Puram in Ayyappa building and thus the accused has found selling duplicate HP toner by infringing the copy right by using the logo and design of HP company and thus the accused has violated the copy right and also cheated the public at large and thereby the accused has committed the offences punishable U/sec. 51(B) 63 of Copy Right Act and Sec.420 of IPC?
2.
What order or sentence?
05. To prove the case, the prosecution has examined in all 5 witnesses as PW.1 to 5 and got marked 5 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.5 and also toners are marked as MO.1.

The prosecution has also not secured the presence of CW.2 and his evidence is also dropped out vide order dated 02.02.2023.
06.
After completion of evidence of prosecution, the incriminating circumstances in the evidence of the prosecution is read over to the accused and statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. recorded.
The accused has denied the incriminating circumstances as false and not chosen to lead his side defence evidence.
07. Heard the arguments.

My findings on the above said points are as follows:-
Point No.1 : In the negative.
Point No.2: As per final order, for the following:
REASONS 08. Points No.1: To prove the case, the prosecution has examined CW.1 as PW.1, he is the authorized officer of HP Company and lodged the complaint and who is identified the cartridges seized from the accused as a duplicate HP toners.
In his evidence, he has deposed that, he has lodged the complaint to the police about the sale of duplicate Samsung and HP company toners near Sajjan Rao Circle, Bengaluru.
He has also deposed about the raid conducted by the police and has deposed that, the accused is not authorized dealer of purchase of HP company.
Thereby, he supported the case of prosecution, but he has not cross examined by the accused side.
09. The prosecution has been examined CW.3, who is the mahazar witness for the seizure mahazar as PW.2.

He has deposed that, on 13.06.2019 CW.6 has called him to the Police Station and in his presence, the CW.6 has conducted the raid and took custody of the accused and seized three toners by drawing mahazar as per Ex.P.2.
He has also deposed that, the accused has shown the godown at Ayyappa building, web way garden, Chikkabasavanapura and from the said godown, CW.6 has seized six duplicate toners.
He has identified the material object as MO.1.

He has also deposed that,
the accused was found selling the toners without any license.
In the cross examination he has deposed that, CW.1 has identified the said toners as duplicate toners.

He has also deposed that,
accused himself opened the godown with the key.
He has also deposed that, they had not any machines to verify whether the toners are duplicate or not.
The said toners are not kept in the box.

Thus, the PW.2 has deposed about the raid conducted by CW.6 and seizure of the toners from the Samir Shaw vs Babu Khan on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111909153/
3 custody of accused by drawing mahazar.
Thus, the evidence of PW.2 is trust worthy evidence, but his evidence can be used as a corroborative evidence when the prosecution has able to prove that the said toners are duplicate toners.
10. The prosecution has been examined police constable who assisted at the time of raid i.e., CW.4 as PW.3.
He has deposed about the raid conducted by CW.6 near Sajjan Rao Circle, Bengaluru and seizure of HP toners.
He has also deposed that, CW.1 has identified the counterfeit/ duplicate cartridges.
He has deposed that, about the conduct of raid at the shop of accused at Ayyappa building, web way garden, Chikkabasavanapura and from the said godown, CW.6 has seized six duplicate toners.
In the cross examination, he has deposed that, the toners are kept in the plastic covers and he has also deposed that, at the time of raid there were no customers for purchase of the cartridges.

Thus, the PW.3 has deposed about the raid conducted by CW.6.
11.
The CW.6 is the Investigating Officer, he is examined as PW.4.
He has deposed about the complaint lodged by CW.1 and register the FIR and deposed about the raid conducted by him in the presence of CW.2 & 3 as mahazar witnesses.

He has deposed that, when he went to Sajjan Rao Circle, Bengaluru, CW.1 shows the person and selling duplicate cartridges of HP and Samsung company and he has took custody of the accused and has seized three HP 12A model toner cartridges from the accused.

He has deposed that, when he visited the godown of the accused at KR Puram along with the accused and has seized 6 toner cartridges of HP 12A model and drawn mahazar and recorded the voluntary statement of the accused and filed the charge sheet.
The Learned Counsel for the accused has not cross examined PW.4 on the date of his examination in chief.
Later the PW.4 is recalled on the application of the accused for cross examination.

But, PW.4 not tendered for cross examination inspite of granting sufficient opportunities and the prosecution has not secured the presence of PW.4.
12.
CW.5/ PW.5 is also the police constable, who assisted CW.6 at the time of raid.
He has deposed about the raid conducted by CW.6 and recovery of HP toners from the custody of accused and drawing of mahazar and also deposed about the raid.

In his cross examination, he has deposed that,
the toners are kept in the plastic covers and he has also deposed that, at the time of raid there were no customers for purchase of the cartridges.
Thus, the evidence of PW.3 & 5 is only to corroborate the evidence of PW.4, who is the Investigating Officer.

13. As discussed above, the PW.1- the complainant and also the person who identified the cartridges seized from the accused as duplicate and the PW.4, who is the Investigating Officer conducted the raid and seized the material from the accused.
But, both are not tendered for cross examination.
Therefore, in the eye of law, there is no evidentiary value of PW.1 & 4.
Therefore, the remaining evidence on record is only the evidence of police constables who assisted CW.4 at the time of raid and seizure of articles.
Even though, these witnesses have deposed about the raid and seizure of toners and there is no record to show that the toners found in the custody of accused are whether duplicate or not.
Further, from the evidence of PW.2 & 3 and 5 it is clear that, the said toners were not in the box and it is kept in the plastic cover.
In this regard, the Learned Counsel for the accused during the arguments he has submitted that, the accused is doing the business of refilling of the cartridges and not selling the cartridges.

He has also insisted that, in the absence of box and only by Samir Shaw vs Babu Khan on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111909153/
4 seeing the cartridges which is in the plastic covers, on that basis it cannot be identify as they are original or duplicate.

Further, It is pertinent to note here that, the PW.1 in his examination in chief has deposed that, ".....
 
 
  
 
  

 
 
   
   
   
   /      

  
   

          
     

 
      

 
   
  
        

      

 
 .....".

But, after careful perusal of Ex.P.1 i.e., complaint wherein it is mentioned that, " ..... our company's products such as Samsung/ HP ink cartridges/ HP toner cartridges etc.,
are being counterfeited by infringing trade mark and copy right marks by some unscrupulous persons in different locations to be named later .......".

But, in Ex.P.2 i.e., panchanama it is mentioned that ".....
 
   
    
    


  
   

    
   


 


    
 
    IKON OUT SOURCING Private Limited              

  
 
  

    
    
   
  

    
       
 
 
 
 

 
  

 
 


    

 
  
......" which clearly reveals that, in Ex.P.1 he mentioned as some unscrupulous persons and in Ex.P.2 he specifically mentioned the name of the accused, which creates doubt regarding the case of prosecution.
Apart from that, in Ex.P.5 i.e., FIR in column No.6 the name of the accused written with the black ink by hand even after its registration online.

Further it is significant to note here that, PW.3 in his cross examination has deposed that, ".....
 
   

    
 

 

    
    
  
 
  



 
   
......".

Whereas after careful perusal of Ex.P.2 panchanama it is mentioned as "......       

   

 
   
  
  
   
  
  ..." which also creates doubt about the case of prosecution.

Further, PW.2 in his cross examination has deposed that, "......
 
    
  
     
   
    
 
 
  
......".

But, PW.3 in his cross examination has deposed that,   
   


    
    
    
  
     
 
 
    . which also creates doubt about the case of prosecution.
Such being so, the benefit of doubt in the case of the prosecution is to be extended to the accused.
Therefore, by extending the benefit of doubt in the case of the prosecution to the accused, this court answers the above Point No.1 in the Negative.
14. Point No.2:-

In view of the findings recorded to the above points, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
By exercising powers conferred U/sec. 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused is acquitted of the offences punishable U/Sec. 51(B), 63 of Copy Right Act and sec. 420 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond of the accused shall continue in force for a period of 6 months.
The accused is set at liberty.
The property reported in PF No.50/2019 marked as MO.1 being cartridges is ordered to be destroyed as worthless after appeal period is over.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and print out taken by her is verified and then pronounced by me in the open court on this the 5th day of October 2024.)
(Sri. Vinod Balnaik.)
IX Addl.Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru City.
